page: Amazon Web Services m8idn.8xlarge is an eighth-generation general-purpose instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features a dedicated x86_64 Intel processor running at up to 3.9 GHz, providing 16 physical cores and 32 vCPUs via multithreading. Memory capacity is configured at 128.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio that allocates 4.0 GB of memory per core. The instance operates without discrete GPU accelerators.

A key architectural aspect of the m8idn.8xlarge is its bundled local storage and networking throughput. It includes 1900 GB of NVMe SSD instance storage for ultra-low latency operations, alongside a 50 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Unlike instances reliant exclusively on network-attached EBS volumes, the direct-attached NVMe storage ensures high-speed scratch space and fast read-write access for ephemeral workloads.

From a resource and cost-efficiency perspective, the inclusion of 1900 GB NVMe storage alongside high baseline networking reduces the overhead of provisioning external high-IOPS block storage arrays. However, because instance store volumes are ephemeral, persistent architectures require replication strategies or secondary EBS provisioning. The m8idn.8xlarge is suited for transactional databases requiring local caches, distributed file systems, high-throughput web serving, and memory-balanced batch data processing pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services m8idn.8xlarge is an eighth-generation general-purpose compute instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. Powered by a 3.9 GHz dedicated Intel x86_64 processor, it offers 16 physical cores and 32 vCPUs paired with 128.0 GB of RAM, preserving a standard 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio. Hardware resources feature 1900 GB of integrated NVMe SSD local storage for high IOPS ephemeral workloads, coupled with a 50 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. It contains no GPU accelerators. The combination of dedicated high-frequency compute, integrated NVMe instance store, and substantial network capacity provides cost-effective throughput for I/O-intensive workloads without relying solely on external block storage. The m8idn.8xlarge is well aligned for mid-tier relational databases, in-memory caching systems with persistence layers, real-time analytics, and network-intensive backend applications.
